findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permissions, oversized file).
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or absent file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and propagate fs::read_to_string with ? or map_err

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a hidden side-effect (stdout logging) inside a function with no Result type. Also contains unchecked indexing parts[0].
findings.failure_mode: side effect leaks into pure-pipeline code, making the function non-deterministic and untestable; index-out-of-range panics if line is malformed
findings.fix: remove println! entirely from this function. If logging is needed, return structured data and log at the call site. Replace parts[0] with parts.get(0).ok_or(ParseError::MissingName)

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() combines unchecked indexing, unchecked parse, and unwrap on fallible operation.
findings.failure_mode: missing second field, non-numeric value, or out-of-range value all panic instead of returning a typed domain error
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingValue) and .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e.to_string())) with proper error propagation

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast that silently truncates values above 65535. parse::<u32>() returns values that may exceed u16::MAX.
findings.failure_mode: a value of 70000 parses successfully then silently becomes 44716, corrupting data with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfRange) or parse directly as u16 if the input range is known

findings.problem: split(',').map(..).collect() collects all parts into a Vec when the grammar is a fixed two-field record. Also uses unchecked parts[0] and parts[1] indexing.
findings.failure_mode: allocates a Vec per line unnecessarily; if a line has fewer than 2 fields, parts[0] and parts[1] panic on out-of-bounds access
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name, rest) in one allocation-free step, then parse rest as the value field

findings.problem: load_tokens mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, and logging in a single function returning Vec<Record> with no error type. The name suggests an I/O action but the return type gives no error surface.
findings.failure_mode: no error type means all failure modes are silenced via unwrap/panic; the function cannot be composed or tested in isolation
findings.fix: split into: (1) pure fn parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError>, (2) fn load_tokens(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that handles I/O and calls parse_line per line with ? propagation

findings.problem: load_tokens returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve for bounded capacity growth. The file line count is known after fs::read_to_string but before collecting.
findings.failure_mode: unbounded reallocation on large files; allocation failure during collect silently panics via Vec growth
findings.fix: after reading text, use text.lines().count() to estimate capacity, call Vec::with_capacity via try_reserve (or use a Result-returning collect pattern), and handle AllocationError

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String instead of a domain newtype. The name field accepts any string with no domain invariants enforced by the type system.
findings.failure_mode: empty names, whitespace-only names, and otherwise invalid names reach the core without validation
findings.fix: introduce a named struct or newtype (e.g., struct Name(String)) with a fallible constructor that validates non-empty, or parse and validate at the boundary before constructing Record

findings.problem: No typed domain error type exists. All failures surface via unwrap panic rather than a structured error enum.
findings.failure_mode: consumer cannot distinguish I/O errors from parse errors from value-out-of-range errors; no recovery is possible
findings.fix: define enum TokenLoadError { Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError), ValueOutOfRange { field: String, value: String } } and return Result<Vec<Record>, TokenLoadError>

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for the token-loading pipeline. The function performs per-line String allocation, trim, clone, and parse — a hot path that needs measured evidence.
findings.failure_mode: unknown whether this is fast enough; cargo-culted allocations (String per field, clone) may dominate throughput
findings.fix: add criterion or tinybench benchmark measuring parse throughput on representative file sizes; use split_once + &str parsing to eliminate intermediate allocations

missing_evidence: no benchmark for the token-loading pipeline throughput
no profiler evidence showing allocation hotspots in load_tokens
no allocation tracing (e.g., mimalloc statistics or jemalloc profiling) for Vec growth behavior
no command output from cargo test to verify behavioral correctness of any fix
no command output from cargo fmt --check or cargo clippy to verify source hygiene
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. All violations are structural: unwrap on I/O and parse, hidden println! side effect, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, split+collect instead of split_once, no error type, and no benchmarks. Every finding is a BLOCKER or MAJOR; the crate cannot be used in production without fixing the unwrap/panic patterns and introducing a Result-based error surface.
